History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
63-year-old man with known heart failure presents with 2-week history of worsening dyspnea and new bilateral ankle swelling, felt to represent an acute decompensation of heart failure; diuretic dose increased and investigations arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive shortness of breath.  
• Onset/Duration: Began gradually ≈2 weeks ago; marked deterioration over the past few days.  
• Course/Progression: Now breathless with minimal exertion (walking to shops, around the house); previously asymptomatic with similar activity.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Mild dry cough.  
  – Bilateral ankle swelling noticed past few days.  
  – No chest pain.  
  – No palpitations, fever, dizziness, or syncope.  
  – Appetite and urinary output unchanged (reports polyuria since starting “the drugs,” presumed diuretic).  
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors: None specified.  
• Review of systems: Otherwise unremarkable as per conversation.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic heart failure (type not specified).  
• History of myocardial infarction (“small heart attack”) 5 years ago; hospitalized for several days, no ongoing chest pain reported since.  
• No other chronic conditions mentioned.

Medications:
• Furosemide – dose/route/frequency not documented (currently once daily; plan to double to twice daily).  
• Aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Bisoprolol – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim).  
• Employment: Part-time lorry (truck) driver; day shifts only.  
• Tobacco: Former smoker, ~1 pack/day for 25 years; quit (date not specified).  
• Alcohol: Denies alcohol use.  
• Exercise: Walks to local shop daily; no vigorous exercise.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction in early 60s.  
• Mother alive with osteoporosis.  
• No other familial cardiac or pulmonary disease reported.

Physical Examination:
(Vital signs and complete examination details not provided in transcript.)  
• Provider states chest examination, oxygen saturations, and blood pressure were “OK.”  
• No other documented findings.

Investigations:
• None completed during visit.  
• Planned:  
  – Blood tests: Full blood count, renal function (urea, creatinine, electrolytes).  
  – Echocardiogram to assess current left-ventricular function (booking within 1–2 weeks).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute decompensation of chronic heart failure  
  • Assessment: Gradual ↑ dyspnea, new peripheral edema, background of CHF; physical parameters currently stable.  
  • Plan:  
    – Increase Furosemide from once daily to one tablet twice daily for several days.  
    – Arrange blood tests (FBC, renal profile).  
    – Schedule echocardiogram.  
    – Review in 1 week to assess symptom response and lab results.  
    – Education: Seek earlier review if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.

Issue 2: Medication monitoring / secondary prevention post-MI  
  • Assessment: On aspirin and beta-blocker; doses not verified.  
  • Plan:  
    – Verify exact doses at next visit; medication reconciliation.  
    – Continue aspirin, bisoprolol.  
    – Consider guideline-directed HF therapies (ACE-I/ARB/ARNI, MRA) once labs available.

General plan items  
  • Reinforce smoking cessation and healthy activity within tolerance.  
  • Discuss occupational impact if symptoms persist.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: Exact vital signs, weight, full cardiovascular/respiratory/abdomen exam, medication doses, current renal function, ACE-I/ARB use, vaccination status.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional connectivity issues caused minor repetition but content understandable.
